content: Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of repaglinide by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of rifabutin by enhancing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin accelerates the metabolism of phenobarbital, leading to reduced phenobarbital levels. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of riociguat by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Limited data suggest that belladonna alkaloids reduce risperidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral formulations. Additionally, belladonna alkaloids antagonize risperidone pharmacodynamically. Both phenobarbital and risperidone increase sedation. Phenobarbital also reduces risperidone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Risperidone enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia. Ritlecitinib increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ritlecitinib inhibits CYP3A4 substrates, increasing their AUC and peak plasma concentrations, which may elevate the risk of adverse reactions. Additional monitoring and dosage adjustments for CYP3A substrates may be required. Belladonna alkaloids and rocuronium both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces ropinirole levels or effects by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Rucaparib increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust CYP2C19 substrate dosages if clinically indicated. Phenobarbital reduces rufinamide levels by enhancing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases ruxolitinib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. This also applies to topical ruxolitinib. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while salmeterol decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Sarilumab may alter CYP450 enzyme formation due to increased cytokine levels, such as IL-6, which can downregulate CYP activity in conditions like rheumatoid arthritis (RA). IL-6 antagonists like sarilumab may reverse this effect, restoring CYP activity and reducing drug concentrations. Exercise caution when initiating or discontinuing sarilumab with CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index. Belladonna alkaloids and scopolamine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and skullcap both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Secukinumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation during chronic inflammation by reducing cytokine levels. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing secukinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index. Phenobarbital reduces selexipag levels or effects by inducing metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Selexipag doses may need to be increased (up to twofold) when coadministered with strong CYP2C8 inducers. Sevelamer increases phenobarbital elimination, reducing its levels. Use caution and monitor. Sevoflurane and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and shepherd's purse both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces silodosin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases sirolimus levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces solifenacin levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Belladonna alkaloids and solifenacin both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. Somapacitan reduces phenobarbital levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Limited data suggest growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated antipyrine clearance. Exercise caution with sensitive CYP substrates. Somatropin reduces phenobarbital levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Limited data suggest growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated antipyrine clearance. Exercise caution with sensitive CYP substrates. Phenobarbital reduces sorafenib levels by enhancing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces sotalol levels by enhancing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Consider higher beta-blocker doses during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Sparsentan increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Sparsentan, a CYP2C19 inducer, reduces exposure and efficacy of CYP2C19 substrates. Stiripentol increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing CYP2C19 substrate doses if adverse reactions occur during coadministration. Phenobarbital reduces streptomycin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and sufentanil both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces sufentanil sublingual effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers may decrease sufentanil levels, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations. Phenobarbital reduces sunitinib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces suvorexant levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease suvorexant efficacy; if dose adjustment is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. Phenobarbital reduces tacrolimus levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces tadalafil levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. For erectile dysfunction patients, monitor tadalafil response carefully due to potential reduced effectiveness. Talquetamab increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Talquetamab may cause cytokine release syndrome (CRS), suppressing CYP enzyme activity and increasing CYP substrate exposure. This is more likely during step-up dosing and up to 14 days after the first treatment dose. Monitor for increased drug concentrations or toxicities of sensitive CYP substrates and adjust doses as needed. Phenobarbital reduces tamoxifen levels or effects by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and tapentadol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces tasimelteon levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Teclistamab increases phenobarbital levels by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Teclistamab induces cytokine release, suppressing CYP450 enzyme activity and increasing CYP substrate exposure. Monitor for increased concentrations or toxicities of sensitive CYP substrates and adjust doses as needed. Tecovirimat increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. Monitor for adverse effects when coadministered with sensitive substrates of these enzymes. Phenobarbital and temazepam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces temsirolimus levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces teniposide levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces terbinafine levels or effects by inducing CYP1A2, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while terbutaline decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Tetracaine and phenobarbital may interact. Use caution and monitor. Monitor for signs of methemoglobinemia when coadministering methemoglobin-inducing drugs. Thalidomide increases phenobarbital effects through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor for increased sedative effects. Phenobarbital reduces theophylline levels or effects by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Thioridazine increases belladonna alkaloid effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids reduce thioridazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral formulations. Belladonna alkaloids also antagonize thioridazine pharmacodynamically. Phenobarbital and thioridazine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and thiothixene both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids reduce thiothixene levels by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Thiothixene increases belladonna alkaloid effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids reduce thiothixene levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral formulations. Phenobarbital reduces tiagabine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids and tiotropium both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces ticagrelor levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Avoid using ticagrelor with potent CYP3A inducers. Phenobarbital reduces timolol levels by enhancing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Consider higher beta-blocker doses during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected than other beta-blockers. Phenobarbital reduces tinidazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces tipranavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces tobramycin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces tofacitinib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Loss of or decreased response to tofacitinib may occur when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inducers. Belladonna alkaloids and tolterodine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Phenobarbital reduces tolterodine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces tolvaptan levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids reduce trifluoperazine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral formulations. Belladonna alkaloids also antagonize trifluoperazine pharmacodynamically. Trifluoperazine increases belladonna alkaloid effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia. Phenobarbital and topiramate both increase sedation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces toremifene levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. CYP3A4 inducers increase toremifene metabolism, lowering steady-state serum concentrations. Phenobarbital and tramadol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor.
